newsletter_description: Invest Newark seeks qualified service providers for small businesses!
description: Invest Newark invites qualified service providers in specific categories to submit their qualifications for inclusion in a directory of service providers. The specific categories of service providers sought support small business owners with: Marketing, Credit Repair, Projection Preparation, Business Coaching, Accounting, Legal Services, and Real Estate (brokers). Qualified respondents will be included in the directory of service providers that Invest Newark may refer to business owners. Additionally, Invest Newark will be issuing grants in 2026 and 2027 that will provide funds for Newark-based small businesses to pay for services in specific categories from qualified service providers. The small businesses - not Invest Newark - will be the clients of selected service providers. This solicitation seeks to build a pool of qualified providers from which grant awardees may select and engage directly.

Once a hotspot for jazz legends—world-class performers filled the stages of this city—it's a landmark destination in jazz history. The torch is carried into the present by organizations like @chickenbonebeachac, preserving our jazz history through concerts, events, and youth camps, and declaring jazz a "progressive, gathering force of inclusion" rather than just musical entertainment. That legacy echoes globally. Since 2011, @unesco has honored jazz annually on April 30. Jazz is peace. Jazz is dialogue. Jazz is freedom. Jazz is that feeling when the music hits and nothing else matters. The times change. The music endures. And Atlantic City? Still Jazzed.

newsletter_description: Join a special conversation with artist David Antonio Cruz at PES Futures!
description: Join us for a special conversation with artist David Antonio Cruz on the occasion of his exhibition black/backroom. Cruz will be joined by PES Co-Directors Jasmine Wahi & Rebecca Pauline Jampol to discuss the exhibition, which continues his unveiling of Queer-Brown-Histories, reflecting on how his work shapes potentialities through intersecting themes of loss, desire, and legacy. Their discussion will contend with how the landscape of art for queer-Brown identities has shifted over the past decade, and in some ways devolved. Looking back at Cruz’s inaugural residency with Project for Empty Space and the coinciding exhibition in 2016, they will consider how Cruz’s practice has evolved while working in community with PES, to underscore how ‘black/backroom’ points toward an abundant future.
performer: David Antonio Cruz, Jasmine Wahi, Rebecca Pauline Jampol

newsletter_description: A refund portal for imported goods tariffs has opened. 80% of importers haven't filed yet!
description: The fed collected $160 billion on imported food and goods over the last year. A refund portal opened this Monday. 80% of importers haven't filed. They have 80 days. Read the fine print. If your goods moved under USMCA, the refund doesn't cover you. If your customs surety paid the tariff, the refund doesn't cover you either. If you filed a protest to protect your money, CBP is now telling you to withdraw it. The portal requires a licensed broker. The clock runs from the moment customs liquidates your entry. Every bottle of olive oil, every sack of dried chiles, every case of Italian tomatoes that fed a New York restaurant paid into this. Sunset Park. Jackson Heights. Chinatown. East Harlem. The Bronx Hub. They took the hit first. The kitchens absorbed it second. The tax is collected from everyone. The refund collects whoever can afford to file. CAPE portal at cbp.gov.3
